messages:
Marie: 03:11 UTC - Customers reporting widespread 5xx and long response time errors for hosted inference EU endpoints. Multiple Zendesk escalations (#1842, #1843). Devon, can you take?

Devon: ack, on it. I can see increase in 502/504s from the edge for /v1/generate. Spike started ~03:09 UTC. Investigating proxies and recent deploys.

incident-bot: ALERT: hosted-eu-gateway-error-rate > 8% (3m), triggered at 03:10:12 UTC.

Sasha: looking at runtime metrics - backend pool for eu-west-1 showing connection queueing and high p95 latency on inference workers. KV-cache miss rate jumped ~x6.

Devon: curl from inside prod: `curl -v https://eu-hosted.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***'` -> `HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway` and upstream: "recv() failed (104: Connection reset by peer)" in the edge logs.

Olivia: infra telemetry shows a burst of auth token refreshes from multiple customers around 03:08-03:10. KMS latency was elevated for a short window (03:07-03:11). Could be auth cache thrash causing backend worker overload.

Andrew: two enterprise customers reported errors during scheduled billing key rotation at 03:05 UTC — might coincide. They hit heavy retry patterns.

Sasha: hypothesis: auth cache TTLs were low after a recent config tweak (30s -> 5s) and combined with KMS hiccup caused a storm of token validation calls, saturating connection pools and increasing backend failures -> 5xx cascade.

Devon: Mitigation attempt 1: increased auth cache TTL on edge from 5s -> 300s (temporary). Observed immediate drop in auth validation QPS. Edge 502 rate down to ~2% within 90s.

Marie: customer comms: posted to affected customers that we're investigating and applied a mitigation; will follow-up with RCA.

Sasha: Mitigation attempt 2: rolled back the config change that reduced cache TTL in the config repo (rolled back 176c2a3). Pushed canary to eu-edge, monitoring. No regressions seen after rollback.

Olivia: Also opened a ticket with KMS provider; they confirmed a transient elevated latency window 03:06-03:12 UTC.

Devon: Post-mitigation status at 03:18: edge error rate ~0.8%, p95 latency back to baseline. No active customer-impacting alerts.

Andrew: Action item for CS: follow up with customers with timeline and temporary workaround notes. I can own comms for the two enterprise customers.

Sasha: Action items for eng-runtime: 1) revert cache TTL config permanently and add a safety check before TTLs < 60s (owner: Sasha, ETA 24h); 2) add circuit breaker on auth validation QPS to shed load when KMS latency spikes (owner: Devon, ETA 48h); 3) add a dashboard for auth validation QPS and KMS latency correlation (owner: Olivia, ETA 72h).

Devon: Also add automated rollback gate for config changes that affect cache behavior (owner: eng-platform, proposal by Sasha, ETA 1 week).

Marie: Support action items: 1) compile affected customer list + ticket IDs and update each ticket with mitigation summary (owner: Marie, ETA 2h); 2) include suggested customer-side retry/backoff guidance (owner: Andrew, ETA 2h).

Sasha: For postmortem: include timeline, root cause (cache TTL + KMS transient), contributing factors (billing rotation retries, lack of auth-QPS circuit), and measurable impact (total affected requests, p95 delta, number of escalations). I'll draft and share by EOD.

Olivia: infra follow-ups: 1) add KMS latency alert sensitivity during peak config changes; 2) validate KMS regional redundancy for auth flows (owner: Olivia, ETA 3 days).

Devon: any outstanding customer repros? I captured one failing request with headers and trace_id `trace-eu-03-9a7c` and attached logs to the ticket. If CS needs more, flag me.

Marie: thanks team. Closing warroom in ~20m; will re-open if new alerts. Postmortem draft expected by EOD with action owners. :thumbsup:

Andrew: Leaving a note for follow-up meeting: propose a runbook step to escalate to dedicated capacity routing when auth-QPS breach detected (reduce blast radius). Added to action list.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: hosted-eu-gateway-error-rate returned to baseline at 03:18:45 UTC.

Devon: leaving the channel but monitoring traces. Ping if anything else pops up.

Sasha: thanks all — will post the postmortem link once drafted.
